findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs changed but is not on the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: The diff changes test_support.rs by 80 lines: EarlyFake gains CI-branch recording and delete_branch. The planned demonstrations listed this file, and the new tests need it. It is test-only code and adds no product scope, but it falls outside the deliverables list.

findings.summary: delete_ci_branch queries the remote even when no push happened (for example a disk hold before the push)
findings.evidence: When produce_and_verify returns Err from hold_for_disk before push_ci_branch, finish_dispatched still calls delete_ci_branch. That does a remote_head lookup (git ls-remote) on a GitHub origin. It is harmless because it finds no branch and deletes nothing, but it costs a network round trip.

summary: The change does what the request asks. After admission, check_and_verify pushes the candidate to athena/ci/<job id> through gh::Remote, before the separate early pull request push. If an earlier run left the branch, the push replaces it, pinned to the head it found. finish_dispatched deletes the branch at close whatever the outcome, including errors. With no GitHub origin, one line says the push is skipped and nothing is pushed. ci.yml now runs on pushes to athena/ci/**, the comment says why, and the job is still named 'fmt, clippy, tests'. I ran the targeted tests and all passed: push then delete in order on success, delete on rejected and failed jobs, nothing pushed and exactly one skip line for five kinds of non-GitHub origin, and failures that cost one warning line without changing the outcome. Every test with a GitHub origin goes through a helper that installs early_seam with recording fakes, so no test reaches the network. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. There are two small findings. test_support.rs changed outside the deliverables list (minor; it was planned and is test-only). The delete step makes a remote lookup even when no push happened (nit).
